chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Asheym, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jowhary, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: A child was born in the era of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who had two heads and two chests in one lower part. So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was asked: 'Does it inherit the inheritance of two or one?' He said: 'Leave it until it sleeps, then shout at it. So if both wake up together, it has the inheritance of one, and if one wakes up and the other remains sleeping, it inherits the inheritance of two.'

key_terms.حَقْوٍ: Lower part / body below the chest

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance determined for a two-headed child in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the application of 'istihsan' (juridical preference) and empirical observation in Shia fiqh, where Imam Ali (AS) uses the state of consciousness as the definitive criterion for individuality rather than anatomical structure alone. It highlights the dynamic nature of legal rulings in early Shia tradition, showing how practical signs (like waking up) determine legal status, a principle that resonates with later discussions on multiple souls in one body.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Ahmad Bin Asheym, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad Al Jowhary, from Hareyz Bin Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘In the era of Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, a child was born and it had two heads for it and two chests in one lower part. So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was asked, ‘Would it inherit two inheritances or one?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Leave it until he goes to sleep, then shout at it. So if both heads wake up together, there would be one inheritance for it, and if one head wakes up and the other one remains sleeping, he would inherit the inheritance of two’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn ’Ashyam from al- Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Jawhariy from Hariz ibn ‘Abd Allah who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that in the time of ’ Amir al-Mu’minin a child was bom with two heads and two chests on one groin.

’ Amir al-Mu’minin was asked about it; if the child receives inheritance for one or for two. He (the Imam) said, ‘The child must be allowed to sleep then called to wake up. If both wake up at the same time the share of inheritance is one share but if one wakes up and the other remains sleeping it then is two shares of inheritance.’” A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Jawhariy from Hariz ibn ‘Abd Allah a similar Hadith.
